title: SN2 mechanism
back: One step, backside attack, transition state with 5 groups, inversion. Rate $=k[\ce{RX}][\ce{Nu-}]$.

title: Enantiomers of butan-2-ol
back: Chiral carbon (four different groups); non-superimposable mirror images; equal mixture = racemic, zero rotation.

title: Finkelstein reaction
back: Works because NaCl and NaBr are insoluble in dry acetone and precipitate.

title: Sandmeyer reaction
back: Diazonium salt to aryl halide with a copper(I) salt.

title: Wurtz, Wurtz–Fittig, Fittig
legend: solvent = dry ether for all three
back: Wurtz: two alkyls. Wurtz–Fittig: aryl + alkyl. Fittig: two aryls.

title: β-Elimination (Zaitsev)
back: Zaitsev: the alkene with more alkyl groups on the double bond is the major product.

title: Reactivity orders
legend: leaving group = I > Br > Cl > F
back: S$_\text{N}$2 is slowed by crowding; S$_\text{N}$1 is speeded by carbocation stability. Allylic and benzylic halides are fast by S$_\text{N}$1.

title: SN1 vs SN2
back: S$_\text{N}$1: two steps, carbocation, rate $k[\ce{RX}]$, 3° fastest. S$_\text{N}$2: one step, rate $k[\ce{RX}][\ce{Nu-}]$, methyl fastest.

title: Why haloarenes resist nucleophiles
back: Resonance gives C–Cl partial double-bond character; $sp^2$ carbon; unstable phenyl cation; ring repels the nucleophile.

title: Aq → alcohol, Alc → alkene
back: Aqueous KOH substitutes; alcoholic KOH eliminates.
